articles.title: Pentagon’s Biggest Battle: Not Iran, But Beards? Hegseth’s Shock Obsession Rocks US Military
articles.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has intensified his crackdown on beards in the U.S. military, ordering stricter enforcement of grooming standards and tighter scrutiny of medical and religious exemptions. The move follows reports that Hegseth was dissatisfied after seeing multiple bearded sailors during a visit to a Navy ship. The Trump administration argues the policy is about discipline, professionalism and military readiness, while critics say the changes could disproportionately affect service members who require beard exemptions for medical conditions such as pseudofolliculitis barbae or for religious reasons. The renewed push has reignited debate over appearance standards across America's armed forces.

articles.description: Fresh questions are being raised about the security of President Donald Trump's recently introduced Qatari-donated Boeing 747 after a report by The New York Times, citing multiple U.S. officials, said the aircraft has not yet been fitted with the advanced anti-missile countermeasure systems installed on the traditional Air Force One fleet. The report says the issue drew attention during Trump's trip to Turkey amid heightened tensions with Iran, with officials deciding the president would return aboard the older Air Force One while the newer aircraft flew separately. During the summit, Trump also said Iran considered him "number one on the list for killing," adding to renewed scrutiny over presidential air security.
